key_insight: The paper replaces hard, deterministic droplet-collision regime boundaries with a probabilistic symbolic model that yields smooth, finite-width transitions between outcomes.
engineering_relevance: This enables more realistic and simulation-ready collision submodels for Eulerian-Lagrangian spray calculations, especially at high ambient pressures relevant to industrial spraying and combustion.
method: Trained a machine-learning teacher on nearly 40,000 experimental collision events across eight regimes and five dimensionless parameters.
Used symbolic regression to distill the learned probability field into eight coupled analytical expressions.
Implemented a "biased-dice" sampling scheme so simulations can sample outcomes consistently from the probabilistic model.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on over 5,000 high-pressure events up to 50 atm and outperformed conventional analytical boundary models.
watch_item: Because the model is probabilistic and multi-regime, correct implementation of the sampling and parameter ranges is important to avoid misusing it outside the validated data domain.
paper_title: Probabilistic Symbolic-Distillation Model of Droplet Collision for Spray Simulation at High Ambient Pressures
